**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects` lists your projec
ts, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists its eval

suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body `{ cod
e, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\n`details` is an

optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or or
phaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant — distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUI
RED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` carries
the parsed challenge. Your key is fine — see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but n
ot allowed to do this — or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJam k
ey will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOU
ND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this write — a
stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_N
OT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests — see [R
ate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The

target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New error c

odes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign

-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts a sign

-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers
 `403 AUTH_REQUIRE
D`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and\n `
resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (the\n
ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (

`source:
 "tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIRED` is
not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server yourself,
upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/i

nspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10*

*.
Exceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables

"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit exceeded. S

low down and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during

the preview.

Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below — carry `Retry-After`
whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather than a gua
rantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may not com

e.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented — request and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playground —

under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog** — discover the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| -
| - |\n| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |\n| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to — where `organ
izationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can
access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /proje
cts/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server info,
recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` |
One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to store,
so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed
since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both values. A field
listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /project
s/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients`
| List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`
| Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client
}/servers` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacement — omitted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{projectI
d}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions (`?pro

jectId=&status=&limit=&before=`) |

**Project environments** — the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
standalone s
erver group, optionally pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval\nsuites and goals run against. Reads need project membership;
**every write\nneeds project admin**. Writes are revisioned: pass the `revision` you last read\nback as `expectedRevision`, and a

stale value returns `CONFLICT` (409) instead
of overwriting a concurrent edit.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET
`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archived ones), or create one
|\n| `GET`, `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment, or edit it (send `null` to clear `
serverAttachmentId`, `skillSelection`, or `pluginVersionIds`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve
` | Preview the host config, closed server set, and pinned plugin versions this environment resolves to right now |\n| `POST /proj
ects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it — reversible, and frees the name for a new one |\n| `POST /pro
jects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/restore` | Restore an archived environment |\n\nArchive and restore are explicit su
b-actions rather than a `DELETE` because the\nrow is kept and restore has real semantics: it re-checks the name and drops\nplugin

pins whose version no longer exists.

**Server diagnostics & primitives** (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`):

|

Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot |
| `POST .
../doctor` | Full health workflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oauth` | Does this server requ
ire an OAuth grant? |\n| `POST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; returns the MCP `
CallToolResult` plus additive `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-i
n-challenges)) |\n| `POST .../prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render a prompt; returns the MCP
